reasoning: Long oo. Collective for walnuts; one walnut is jooze. The same form also means a pair and, in dialect, a husband.
ص is emphatic S, which backs the word and makes the taa marbuta come out a. The customary reconciliation between families, as against plain Sul7 for peace.
Long ee in the dual-shaped ending. In speech it almost always carries the article, il-ba7reen.
Clipped form of allah ya3Tiik il-3aafye. m3allim is the friendly Palestinian address to a tradesman or shopkeeper, with the shadda doubling the l.

The English says to a woman, so the verb is second-person feminine rajja3ti plus -li, which lengthens to rajja3tiili; the Arabic is respelt with ي to show it. ط is a sun letter and emphatic, giving iT-Tanjara.
jeebe, from French jupe, is a skirt in Palestinian. A pocket is jeeb جيب without the taa marbuta.
Covers both cause and purpose, as the English says. Often shortened to 3ashaan before a pronoun or clipped to 3a-.
The frame is la X wala Y, as in la haad wala hadaak. The ellipsis in the headword marks the slot and is not romanized.
The stopcock on a water or gas line, as in sakkir il-ma7bas. The same word is also used for a wedding or engagement ring, so context decides.
Singulative of the collective naamuus; taa marbuta after س is e. barghash is a near synonym for gnats.
Taa marbuta after ر is a. Used for work experience, as in 3indo khibra.
A media and sports term, so ق keeps [q] here; the construct makes the taa marbuta -et, written ت for the voice. In casual talk people just say footbol or Taabe for the ball.
A clipped version of la 7awla wala 'uwwata illa billah, said at bad news or exasperation. The vowel in 7awl keeps the MSA diphthong because the phrase is a fixed religious quotation.
A fixed proverb of MSA shape that Ramallah speakers quote as it is; ط is a sun letter so the article assimilates, and ق is glottalised in the dialect delivery.
heek with a long ee is the Palestinian so or like that. This is the default way to say therefore in Ramallah.
ظ is the emphatic interdental, written TH, and the shadda doubles it. Form II past, he cleaned.
Taa marbuta after م is e; plural zlaam. Everyday Palestinian for a man, and ya zalame is a common address.
Form II tammam with the -lak indirect object. Said about a wedding, a trip or anything under way; kheer has a long ee.
Form X verbal noun, used in ordinary talk about fuel and electricity bills. The t and h are separate letters here, not a digraph.
ق is a glottal stop and the n is doubled in Palestinian, 'anniine; the headword spelling omits the shadda. Typically a glass bottle.
The middle vowel drops in speech, il-faat7a; ف is a moon letter. Most often heard in i'ra il-faat7a 3ala roo7o.
Form V participle with the medial hamza written '; the shadda doubles خ, written khkh. Used of a person being late and of a late hour.
ق glottalises; long uu in the intensive CaCuuC pattern. 7aa'id is the more everyday way to describe someone who holds a grudge.
khalliini plus a bare subjunctive is the Palestinian let me. Both hamzas inside at'akkad are written; the shadda doubles the k.
Long aa then long ee. Used both spatially and for approximate quantities, 7awaaleen 3ashar da'aayi'.
